title: Former iPhone display plant in Japan to start new life in chip supply chain
source_used: Nikkei Asia (subscription; headline, standfirst and opening paragraph only) and Digitimes (publisher preview)
key_facts: Nikkei Asia standfirst: JDI's Mobara factory will churn out package substrates for its fifth owner, Shinko Electric.
The Mobara plant made LCDs for iPhones, but Apple later switched to a different display technology.
Nikkei Asia calls it a factory that once carried the hopes of Japan's display industry, to be reborn under its fifth owner.
Digitimes preview: Shinko Electric Industries plans to convert the site into a production base for semiconductor package substrates used in AI applications.
quote_evidence: JDI's Mobara factory to churn out package substrates for fifth owner Shinko Electric
The Mobara plant made LCDs for iPhones, but Apple later switched to a different display technology.

A former iPhone display factory in Mobara, Japan, is set for a new role in the semiconductor supply chain, with Shinko Electric Industries planning to convert the site into a production base for semiconductor package substrates used in artificial intelligence (AI) applications.
why_it_matters_hint: AI chips need package substrates, the base boards that carry a chip, so a new Japanese plant would add a source of them; investment size, start date and output are not known.
notes: Nikkei Asia is subscription-only; only the headline, standfirst and first paragraph were visible. Digitimes carries the same story (preview only). No numbers, dates or investment size available.
